nature.description: Forests, waterfalls, lakes and wide valleys, photographed and painted, for phone and desktop screens.
nature.intro:
Our Nature collection gathers the places people go to slow down: forest paths in morning light, waterfalls tumbling into green pools, misty lakes, river valleys and the last glow of a sunset over open water. Most of it is real photography, from Croatia's Krka falls to the slopes around Mount Fuji, with a handful of painted and dreamlike landscapes mixed in for when you want something softer.

Nature images make some of the most forgiving wallpapers. The textures are busy enough to look rich but rarely fight with your icons, and greens and blues stay easy on the eyes through a long day. For a phone, pick a portrait shot with a clear subject in the upper half, so the clock and widgets sit on calmer sky or water. On a desktop, wide valley and lake scenes fill a monitor without an awkward crop. Every wallpaper lists its exact resolution, so you can choose one that matches your screen.

architecture.description: Modern facades, grand interiors and striking structures from around the world.
architecture.intro:
The Architecture collection is for anyone who likes clean lines and good light. You'll find glass towers in Tallinn, the white curves of Valencia's City of Arts and Sciences, arched halls, quiet modern interiors with big windows and minimalist furniture, and facades photographed so tightly they turn into patterns.

Buildings work well as wallpapers because they bring structure to a screen. Strong verticals suit phones, where a single tower or column draws the eye up past your apps, while wide interiors and skylines suit desktops and laptops. Light-coloured facades against a blue sky give a bright, airy home screen; dusk shots and lit-up interiors are better if you use dark mode. More than half of this collection is in portrait format, so it is one of the best places on Aurora to find a sharp, uncluttered phone background.

hinduism.description: Devotional art of Krishna, Radha, Shiva and other deities, in traditional and modern styles.
hinduism.intro:
This collection brings together devotional art from Hindu tradition, made with care for those who like to keep their faith close at hand. Krishna appears most often: playing the flute beneath a tree, crowned with a peacock feather, beside Radha, or guiding Arjuna on the chariot at Kurukshetra. You'll also find Lord Shiva, meditative compositions and traditional Indian motifs, in styles that range from classic painting to bold modern digital art.

Nearly all of these wallpapers are portrait, made for phone lock and home screens, where a devotional image can be the first thing you see each morning. Paintings with warm golds and deep blues read well behind white clock text, while the darker neon and silhouette pieces suit dark mode. If a deity's face is the focus, choose an image where it sits in the upper or middle third so your icons don't cover it. Every image is shown at its full resolution on its page, so you can check it will look sharp on your phone.

dark.description: Moody, shadowy and atmospheric wallpapers made for dark mode and OLED screens.
dark.intro:
Dark wallpapers are about mood: fog over railway tracks at night, cloaked figures in empty halls, lone silhouettes against fire, eerie forests and small bright details against deep black. This collection leans cinematic and a little gothic, with plenty of quieter, near-black images for people who simply want their screen to recede.

There is a practical side too. On phones and laptops with OLED displays, black pixels are switched off, so a mostly dark wallpaper can save a little battery and looks especially deep. Dark backgrounds also keep white icons and text crisp and are kinder to your eyes at night. If you want contrast without clutter, look for images with one lit subject, such as a glowing window, a pair of eyes or a single flower, and plenty of empty shadow around it. You'll find both portrait phone versions and wide desktop scenes here.

abstract.description: Fluid shapes, 3D renders, gradients and painterly abstracts in every colour.
abstract.intro:
Abstract wallpapers give you colour and movement without a subject to get in the way. This collection mixes glossy 3D renders made in Blender, swirling fluid shapes, gradient diamonds, painted ocean-wave textures and surreal compositions that sit somewhere between art and illustration.

Because there is no horizon or face to crop around, abstracts adapt to almost any screen shape, which makes them a safe pick for foldables, tablets and ultrawide monitors. Choose by colour first: soft gradients and pastel waves stay calm behind busy home screens, while high-contrast neon swirls make a statement on a lock screen that is otherwise empty. If you match your phone case, laptop or desk setup, try searching Aurora by colour, for example "purple" or "teal", and then narrow down here.

minimal.description: Clean, simple wallpapers with lots of space: single objects, soft shapes and quiet rooms.
minimal.intro:
Minimal wallpapers do more with less: a single dome, one curved 3D shape on black, a quiet desk, a shelf, an empty room with a bed in the corner, or a tree branch drawn in a few lines. The idea is a background that feels designed rather than decorated, leaving room for your icons and widgets to breathe.

A good minimal wallpaper has one focal point and plenty of negative space, usually off-centre so it isn't hidden behind a clock or dock. Light versions suit bright, airy home screens; black-background renders pair well with dark mode and OLED displays. Minimal images are also the easiest to live with long term, because there is nothing in them to grow tired of. If you like this style, our article on why less is more explains what separates a great minimal wallpaper from an empty one, and the Gradient and Geometric collections are good next stops.

neon.description: Glowing signs, light tunnels and night streets lit in pink, blue and purple.
neon.intro:
The Neon collection is lit from within: glowing shop signs on brick walls, light tunnels, glitch-art lettering, night streets washed in pink and blue, and silhouettes framed by tubes of coloured light. Some are real photographs from cities like Tokyo and Paris; others are digital art that pushes the glow further than any street could.

Neon works best on dark backgrounds, which makes it a natural match for dark mode. The bright lines draw the eye, so choose an image where the main glow sits away from where your clock or app icons appear. Pink and purple neon feels warm and retro; cyan and blue feel cooler and more futuristic. Most of this collection is in portrait format for phones. If you want a whole city in neon rather than a single sign, have a look at our Cyberpunk collection too.

space.description: Nebulae, galaxies, planets and spacecraft, from telescope imagery to space art.
space.intro:
Space wallpapers range from the real to the imagined. This collection includes nebulae and galaxies captured by telescopes and amateur astronomers, night skies over salt lakes and mountains, close-ups of spacecraft cockpits and stations, and space art of black holes, portals and planets that no camera has seen.

Space images suit almost any screen because they are mostly dark with points of colour, so icons and text stay readable. Deep-field star images look especially good on OLED phones and laptops, where black is truly black. Telescope images come in many shapes; for a phone, choose a portrait crop where the brightest part of the nebula sits in the middle, and for a desktop, pick a wide panorama so the scene isn't stretched. Most of this collection is wide format for monitors and laptops. Each wallpaper's page shows its full resolution and similar images, so it's easy to find a matching set.

mountains.description: Snow-capped peaks, alpine meadows and dramatic ridgelines at every hour of the day.
mountains.intro:
From the Dolomites and the Himalaya to Mount Fuji and the Mahabharat range, the Mountains collection is all about scale. You'll find snow-capped peaks under clear blue skies, ridgelines fading into haze at dusk, hikers crossing summer meadows, and sunrise light catching the highest summits.

Mountains make classic desktop wallpapers: the horizon sits low, leaving open sky across the top for icons and windows. For phones, pick a portrait image where the peak rises into the upper half, or a layered ridge scene that reads well when cropped. Blue-hour and dusk shots pair nicely with dark mode, while bright daytime peaks keep a home screen fresh. Since mountain photos are detailed, resolution matters, so check that the size on the wallpaper's page is at least your screen's size to avoid any softness.

ocean.description: Waves, shorelines and open water, from aerial beach views to stormy seas.
ocean.intro:
The Ocean collection captures water in all its moods: aerial views of waves breaking on black-sand beaches, calm twilight horizons, rocky shores, curling waves caught mid-break and a tall ship riding out a storm. There are real photographs from coastlines like Australia's Mornington Peninsula alongside a few stylised and painted seascapes.

Ocean images are naturally calming, and their blues and teals sit comfortably behind most icon sets. Aerial shots, where the shoreline makes a strong line across the frame, look striking on wide desktop screens. Horizon shots with plenty of sky work well when you need space for widgets. All the wallpapers in this collection are currently in landscape format, so they're best suited to monitors, laptops and tablets held sideways. For more water scenes, try the Nature and Sunset collections.

sci-fi.description: Science-fiction and fantasy art: spacecraft, futuristic worlds, dragons and lone heroes.
sci-fi.intro:
Sci-Fi gathers art from imagined worlds: futuristic corridors and spacecraft, armoured sentinels, volcanic abysses, dragons circling ancient ruins, phoenixes rising and lone figures facing something far bigger than themselves. It mixes classic science fiction with fantasy, in painted and digital art styles.

These wallpapers tend to be detailed and dramatic, so they shine on large desktop and laptop screens where you can see everything. Most of the collection is in wide format for that reason. If you use one on a phone, choose a scene with a clear central subject, such as a helmet, a ship or a creature, so the important part survives the crop. Darker scenes with glowing highlights also look great in dark mode. For more futuristic cityscapes, see Cyberpunk, and for real nebulae and planets, see Space.

city.description: Skylines, streets and city lights by day and night, from New York to Trondheim.
city.intro:
The City collection looks at urban life from every angle: New York seen from a helicopter, Chicago's skyline in night fog, blue hour over downtown streets, reflections in Trondheim's harbour, lantern festivals, quiet lanes and busy crossings. There is a strong lean towards evening and night, when city lights turn ordinary streets into something cinematic.

Skylines are great desktop wallpapers because the buildings sit low and leave sky for your icons. Street-level and vertical shots, of which there are many here, suit phone screens well. Night photos pair naturally with dark mode, while daytime shots feel brighter and more open. If you want a particular city, try searching Aurora for its name. For a more futuristic take on the city, our Neon and Cyberpunk collections are close neighbours.

cyberpunk.description: Rain-soaked neon streets, dystopian skylines and futuristic tech.
cyberpunk.intro:
Cyberpunk is the city of the future seen at night: rain on neon-lit streets, narrow alleyways glowing pink and blue, dystopian skylines, robotic heads and storefronts humming with light. The collection mixes real night photography that feels futuristic with digital art that goes all the way into science fiction.

Cyberpunk images are rich, detailed and dark, which makes them ideal for desktops, laptops and ultrawide monitors, where the depth of a street scene really opens up. Almost all of this collection is in wide format. Their dark tones with bright accents also keep icons and text easy to read, and they look excellent on OLED displays. If you prefer a single glowing sign rather than a full scene, see the Neon collection; for spaceships and other worlds, try Sci-Fi.

cats.description: Curious kittens, sleepy cats and feline illustrations for phone and desktop.
cats.intro:
A collection for cat people: curious kittens peeking over ledges and from behind stones, calico and tabby cats resting on garden paths, blue-eyed portraits that look straight at you, and a few playful illustrations, from a sleeping cartoon cat to a parade in the park.

Most of these wallpapers are portrait, made for phone screens, which is where a pet photo tends to live. Close-up portraits with soft, blurred backgrounds are the easiest to use, because the background stays calm behind your icons while the face stays in view. Choose an image where the cat's eyes sit in the upper half of the frame so your clock doesn't cover them. Whether you have a cat of your own or just wish you did, there's an expression here to make you smile every time you unlock your phone.

floral.description: Roses, dahlias, daisies and hydrangeas in close-up, from soft pastels to dark moody blooms.
floral.intro:
The Floral collection is close-up and colourful: dewy red roses, peach and yellow dahlias, pink gerbera daisies against blue, hydrangeas in moody light, orange blooms glowing out of dark surroundings and a few painterly flower artworks. Some are bright and fresh; others are dark and dramatic, with a single bloom lit against deep green or black.

Flower close-ups make lovely phone wallpapers, and most of this collection is portrait for that reason. Soft-focus images with blurred backgrounds give icons a calm base, while dark-background blooms pair well with dark mode and make the colour pop. For a lock screen, choose a flower that sits in the lower half of the frame so the clock floats above it. If you like these, the Nature and Minimal collections have more quiet, botanical images.

cars.description: Supercars, classics and tuned cars, from race tracks to car meets.
cars.intro:
The Cars collection is for anyone who stops to look when something special drives by. You'll find supercars lined up at track days, a blue Huracán on a racing circuit in Noida, doors raised on green and orange sports cars, tuned Audis at European car meets, and classic muscle and vintage cars with their bonnets open.

Car photos are wide by nature, so this whole collection is in landscape format, ideal for desktops, laptops and tablets held sideways. Side and three-quarter shots fill a monitor beautifully; head-on shots are bold and symmetrical. If you want your icons to stay readable, pick an image where the car sits in the lower half of the frame with clear tarmac or sky above. Every wallpaper's page lists its exact resolution, so you can find one that is sharp on a large or high-resolution monitor.

geometric.description: Clean patterns, receding stripes and 3D geometric shapes.
geometric.intro:
Geometric wallpapers are built from shape and repetition: black and white stripes receding into the distance, glass roof frames, warm interlocking blocks, faceted gems and intersecting lines. Many are crisp 3D renders made in Blender, designed specifically as phone wallpapers.

Patterns are some of the most practical wallpapers you can use, because there is no single subject to hide behind icons and they look tidy on any screen. Fine, regular patterns read best on high-resolution phones, while bolder, larger shapes suit desktops and tablets. Warm oranges and reds feel energetic; monochrome stripes feel calm and modern. Most of this collection is portrait, made for phones. For softer colour without hard edges, see Gradient, and for more sculptural renders, see Abstract.

gradient.description: Smooth colour blends and light leaks that stay out of your icons' way.
gradient.intro:
Gradient wallpapers are pure colour: smooth blends from one hue to another, soft light leaks, gentle swirls and hazy fades. They are the simplest wallpapers on Aurora and among the most useful, because they never compete with what's on your screen.

A gradient works on any device and any layout, so it's a good choice if you use lots of widgets or simply want your home screen to feel calm. Warm sunset blends feel cosy, cool blues and purples feel modern, and darker gradients pair well with dark mode. Gradients also make it easy to match a phone case, a theme or your mood, and to switch with the seasons. Almost all of this collection is portrait for phones. If you want a little more texture, try Abstract; for clean lines, see Geometric.

sunset.description: Golden hours, silhouettes and fiery skies over cities, seas and mountains.
sunset.intro:
Sunset collects the hour when the light turns gold: silhouettes standing in fields, the sun sinking over South African plains and city skylines, ice glowing pink at dusk, stormy skies over highways and fantasy landscapes bathed in orange. There are also a few starry skies for after the sun goes down.

Sunset images are warm and immediately calming, and their horizons make them natural desktop wallpapers, with the bright band of sky sitting behind your open windows. Most of this collection is in wide format for monitors and laptops. Silhouette shots, where the foreground is pure black against colour, also work well in dark mode and keep icons readable. For a phone, choose an image with a tall sky so the colour fills the screen above your apps.

forest.description: Misty pines, autumn canopies and quiet woodland paths.
forest.intro:
The Forest collection is quiet and atmospheric: tall pines disappearing into mist, bare winter trees in fog, autumn leaves seen from below, a lone walker on a calm woodland path, and starry skies over the treetops. Some scenes are bright and colourful; many are dark and moody, the kind of forest that feels a little enchanted.

Most of these wallpapers are portrait, because tall trees fit a phone screen naturally, leading your eye from the ground up through the canopy. Misty, low-contrast images make particularly good home screens since nothing in them fights with your icons. Darker forest scenes suit dark mode and OLED displays, while autumn colours bring warmth to a lock screen. For wider landscapes with forests and lakes, see the Nature and Mountains collections.
